question: A 71-year-old man presents to his primary care physician with complaints of fatigue, weight loss, and early satiety for 3 weeks. Before this, he felt well overall. He is a former smoker, but otherwise has no past medical history. On examination, the patient appears fatigued and thin; his stool is guaiac positive. He is referred to a gastroenterologist who performs an esophagogastroduodonoscopy that reveals a mass in the antrum of the stomach. Pathology consistent with adenocarinoma. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management:?

options.opc: Obtain CEA, CA 125 antigen, and CA 19-9

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, and early satiety" -> "Suspicion of gastrointestinal malignancy" -> "Esophagogastroduodenoscopy performed" -> "Mass in the antrum of the stomach identified" -> "Pathology consistent with adenocarcinoma" -> "Consider staging for cancer" -> "Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Adenocarcinoma in the antrum of the stomach" -> "Need for accurate staging" -> "Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) for local staging" -> 85%
enhanced_information: The most appropriate next step in management for a 71-year-old man with adenocarcinoma in the antrum of the stomach is to perform an Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) for accurate local staging, as per standard practice guidelines.
analysis: The core medical principle in the management of gastric adenocarcinoma involves accurate staging to guide treatment decisions. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) is the most appropriate next step for local staging in this scenario, as it provides detailed information about the depth of tumor invasion and regional lymph node involvement. This aligns with standard practice guidelines for gastric cancer management.
